text:
sasha: FYI support escalated a P1 from Acme at 04:12 UTC — p99 for chat generation jumped from ~220ms -> ~1.1s after last night's kernel rollout. customer seeing timeouts in prod.
kevin: ack, can you post trace/id and affected model?
sasha: model=redwood-chat-3b-v2, rollout-id=deploy-2026-03-16-keropt, trace id=trace_0a7f. Logs show a lot of SDPA->generic fallback switches and long kernel compile times.
mira: that rollout touched compile flags: ENABLE_SDP_ACCEL=1 and ATTEN_KERNEL_HINT=auto -> also changed nvcc flags to -O3 -ftz.
jordan: timeline: deploy started 03:50 UTC, first anomalies ~04:05, support ticket at 04:10. p95 also drifted but p99 jumped most.
sasha: attached stack snippet from the trace (truncated):
```
[sdpa_kernel_select] preferred=sdpa, compiled=false -> fallback=generic_attn
[kernel_compile] compile_time=5.2s, post_compile_landing=bad
[exec] token_latency=120ms per-batch -> 560ms
```
kevin: can we force the runtime to prefer FlashAttention kernel for that model as a mitigation?
mira: yes, runtime supports per-model kernel preference. Command: `curl -X PATCH https://control.internal/api/models/redwood-chat-3b-v2 -H 'Auth: token' -d '{"kernel_pref":"flash_attn"}'`
jordan: before we flip, is there any correctness difference? we have tests but want to avoid hallucination regressions.
kevin: flash_attn path is functionally identical for this arch; SDPA was supposed to be faster but fallback/unexpected compile jank is causing p99.
sasha: support asked for repro steps for internal postmortem. I pushed a small script to reproduce under load: `scripts/repro_p99.sh` — it runs 200 concurrent short-chat requests with seq_len=512.
ops-bot: NOTE: canary pool for deploy-2026-03-16-keropt currently has 12 instances in us-west1, health=70%.
mira: quick mitigations: 1) set kernel_pref flash_attn for affected model, 2) revert ATTEN_KERNEL_HINT to previous static value, 3) disable compile-on-demand (precompile kernels during maintenance window).
jordan: prioritized steps: (A) temporary kernel_pref flip, (B) roll back compile flags in a canary, (C) run perf/cupti traces to get nvrtc failures.
kevin: i applied kernel_pref=flash_attn to redwood-chat-3b-v2 in us-west1 canary — rollout id kflip-176833. Watch p99.
sasha: support update sent to Acme: "we are toggling kernel preference to mitigate latency; will follow up with RCA." they marked incident as high impact.
mira: running couple of repro runs now. initial canary p99 dropped from 1.1s -> 260ms. good signal.
kevin: digging into compile logs: `/var/log/attn_compile.log` shows repeated nvrtc OOMs and falling back to generic. error snippet: `nvrtc: failed to allocate 2147483648 bytes` — indicates memory pressure during JIT compile.
jordan: could this be due to increased batch size in last config? workload hasn't changed on customer side. maybe kernel codegen produced larger kernels.
mira: hypothesis: -ftz and -O3 exposed a codepath that increases kernel memory. revert will reduce compile memory footprint.
kevin: action items assigned: mira -> open rollback PR for compile flags and run canary; jordan -> collect nvprof/cupti traces and seq_len histogram; sasha -> keep support loop tight with customer and post updates; oncall -> watch for collateral impact.
on-text: reaction :thumbsup: (mira)
ops-bot: ALERT: canary kflip-176833 reached 90% healthy, p99 restored to baseline.
oncall: scheduling 30m postmortem at 09:00 UTC to capture root cause and prevention (precompile, memory limits for nvrtc).
sasha: also adding a short-term guard: autoset `compile_max_memory=1GB` and `compile_retry_delay=30s` to avoid noisy JIT storms.
kevin: long term: add offline kernel building for common seq_len buckets and a kernel cache invalidation policy tied to compile flag changes.
jordan: +1. will draft the postmortem notes and include commit ids, affected hosts, and exact timing.
sasha: closing loop: customer acknowledged mitigation and will run smoke tests. leaving thread open for postmortem artifacts.
